messages:
miriam: quick heads-up — we rolled quant-boot-v1 (PTQ int8) into the onboarding canary this morning. initial pass vs our funcall schema suite shows parse-fail rate ~3.7% vs float baseline ~0.6% :grimacing:
raj: ugh, that's higher than expected. is it concentrated on a particular schema or across the board? :eyes:
miriam: looks skewed to arrays and nested objects in tool outputs. single-field toolcalls mostly fine. example failing output below from a canary sample:
```
{"tool":"price_lookup","result":"[{\"sku\":\"A-123\",\"price\":\"$12.00\"}]"}
```
(suffix truncated and mismatched brackets)
sylvia: that example looks like the decoder is dropping trailing tokens mid-struct — could be kv-cache boundary or tokenization differences after quantization. any differences in eos handling?
miriam: seq-len distribution same. observed a lot of early eos tokens in int8 traces. also saw higher alt-token probability at tail.
raj: can we repro locally with the exact PTQ artifact and the same prompt batch? if yes, bisect between float -> per-layer quant -> full PTQ.
miriam: repro script ready. running small bisect now, will push logs to /tmp/ptq-parse-debug.log and link.
ops-bot: deploy: canary group updated -> quant-boot-v1 @ 08:12 UTC. 1200 requests routed.
kevin: timeline-wise we should consider fallback to float for routes with >1% parse-fail SLA breach. better to auto-failover than escalate to incidents.
sylvia: agree. short-term mitigation ideas:
- increase retry budget for schema parsing to allow json-rescue heuristics
- apply light postprocess "json-healer" that fixes simple suffixes (closing braces, bracket balancing)
- route arrays-heavy prompts to float model by routing rule based on route metadata
raj: json-healer helps but masks real quality regression. important to collect two signals: raw parse-fail and healed-accept rate so we can alert on regressions even if healed.
miriam: added telemetry plan: emit metric `funcall.parse.raw_fail` and `funcall.parse.healed_ok` with tags {model_variant, canary=true/false, route}. also spike alert if raw_fail > 1% for 10m.
kevin: sounds good. can we do a quick AB: 50% requests go to int8 + healer, 25% to int8 raw (no healer), 25% to float? that splits signal and reduces blast radius.
sylvia: yes. I can add a rollout config:
```
rollout:
  groups:
    - name: int8_heal
      pct: 50
      model: quant-boot-v1
      postprocess: json-healer
    - name: int8_raw
      pct: 25
      model: quant-boot-v1
      postprocess: none
    - name: float_baseline
      pct: 25
      model: float-boot-v2
      postprocess: none
```
miriam: running AB now. starting to collect: raw_fail int8_heal ~3.6%, int8_raw ~3.8%, float_baseline ~0.5% (first 5k requests). healer converts ~65% of raw fails into healed_ok but we need to check semantic correctness of healed outputs.
raj: for semantic checks, let's sample 200 healed outputs and run evals against the canonical tool contract tests. put in a queue for human review + automated similarity check.
kevin: also file a quick rollback play: if raw_fail_int8_raw > 2% for 30m OR healed_ok false_negative rate > 10% then revert traffic to float.
miriam: creating ticket: ENGML-4821 with links to logs and AB dashboard. PR to add healed telemetry and AB rollout config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/849
sylvia: one more thought — quant kernel selection might be swapping a fast but lower-precision kernel at tail positions. we'll run kernel-level compare with token-prob diffs. raj can you add a probe to dump last-32 token logits for a small sample set?
raj: on it. dumping to s3://redwood-canary/ptq-logits/1767639999/ and will attach to ticket.
miriam: next steps checklist:
- raj: kernel-level probes + logits dump (ETA 2h)
- sylvia: rollout config + json-healer + telemetry (ETA 1h)
- kevin: define failover SLO and rollback rule (ETA 30m)
- miriam: sampling and human review queue config (ETA 3h)
if no major regression in 6h we keep canary, else rollback and notify enterprise customers.
kevin: thanks team. keep updates short here. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: alert: funcall.parse.raw_fail rate exceeded threshold in canary group int8_raw (3.9%) at 08:58 UTC — paging suppressed (info).
